slots.hypothesis: Core is the daily intraday money-flow tilt: (Amt-weighted minute return minus equal-weighted minute return) / intraday std. It is the kernel of the only clean head (+0.61, valid +2.61, sign +1). That head has only been grown with pure time smoothing ({cross_mean}, {cross_ema}). The level of the tilt mixes a stable per-stock intraday composition (open/close U-shape, closing-auction share; the r1 auditor's competing explanation) with real flow information. The new peripheries leave smoothing and use five families. (1) Abnormal tilt relative to the stock's own history (GKM 2001), which removes the persistent composition part by construction. (2) Cross-day Amt-weighted minus equal-weighted tilt, plus covariance with the amount z-score (busy days vs normal days). (3) A per-stock informativeness term, cross_corr(lagged tilt, daily return, 120), alone and times the recent tilt (LMSW 2002 classification; Easley et al. 2002). (4) Persistence and continuity: autocorrelation-weighted tilt (Chordia-Subrahmanyam 2004 order splitting) and a frog-in-the-pan rank difference (Da-Gurun-Warachka 2014). (5) Tail asymmetry and tilt relative to the day's direction. No powers of volume or volatility and no cs_* fed a cross-sectional constant. 13 seeds are kept deliberately far from the +0.61 head to avoid the |rho|>=0.7 strike. Direction is left to the reward. Why it should last out of sample: the head is stronger in valid than in train; order splitting, T+1 and short-sale limits are structural; every periphery is a per-stock relative quantity.

Overnight vs intraday tug of war (Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019, Berkman et al. 2012, Qiao-Dam 2020 on the A-share T+1 overnight discount, Jiang-Luo-Ye 2023-05, Aboody et al. 2018). Retail decisions after the close and at the opening auction set the overnight segment; institutions set the intraday segment. Which segment a stock's recent return came from says who is pushing the price, which the 20-day reversal control cannot see because it is the sum of the two segments. Operators: r_on = log(open / previous close) and r_id = log(close / open). They give (1) overnight drift scaled by the stock's own volatility (20/60-day mean, EMA, and 5-day minus 60-day abnormal overnight return); (2) cs_bucket_rank of the overnight mean within same-total-return deciles, orthogonal to reversal by construction; (3) per-stock tug-of-war strength via cross_corr / cross_regbeta of r_on against r_id, and yesterday's r_id against today's r_on; (4) where price discovery happens: overnight share of absolute moves, the overnight/intraday volatility ratio, and the signed opening-auction amount share. All terms are scale-free. None is a level or power of a control, and none feeds a constant to cs_*. No head reads a time split of returns, and the +1.53 head uses only the opening-price level as a top-10% flag. Direction is left to the reward. Why it should last out of sample: it comes from institutions and investor clienteles (T+1, call auctions) that did not change after the sample. Known risk noted: the 2018-08 SSE closing-auction reform.
